questions.question: Which of the following statements related to MS Word 365 is/are correct? 1) ‘Save’ allows you to update a previously saved file with new content. 2) ‘Save As’ allows you to save a new file or an existing file to a new place with the same name or a different name.
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following statements related to MS Word 365 is/are correct?

1) ‘Save’ allows you to update a previously saved file with new content.

2) ‘Save As’ allows you to save a new file or an existing file to a new place with the same name or a different name.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both (1) and (2).

Key Points

  • 'Save' allows you to update a previously saved file with new content. This means any changes made to the document will be stored in the same file without creating a new file.
  • 'Save As' allows you to save a new file or an existing file to a new place with the same name or a different name. This is useful when you want to keep the original file unchanged and create a new file with the changes.
  • MS Word 365 is a part of the Microsoft Office 365 suite that includes a range of tools for document creation, editing, and collaboration.
  • Using 'Save' and 'Save As' appropriately can help manage versions of documents and ensure important data is not overwritten unintentionally.

Additional Information

  • Save:
    • The 'Save' function in MS Word updates the last saved version of the document with the current changes made.
    • This command is used when you are working on a document and want to ensure that all recent changes are stored in the same file.
    • The shortcut for 'Save' is Ctrl + S (Windows) or Command + S (Mac).
  • Save As:
    • The 'Save As' function allows you to save the document in a different location, with a different name, or in a different format.
    • This is particularly useful when you want to create a copy of the document and retain the original.
    • It also allows saving the document in formats compatible with other software or older versions of MS Word.
    • The shortcut for 'Save As' is F12 (Windows) or Shift + Command + S (Mac).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of communication on the internet?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of communication on the internet?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is It is always private.

Key Points

  • Communication on the internet is not always private because online interactions can be subject to surveillance, hacking, data breaches, or monitoring by third parties.
  • Many platforms and services collect user data for analytics, personalization, and advertising, which compromises privacy.
  • Activities like email exchanges, social media interactions, and file sharing often involve third-party servers or intermediaries, which can access or store data.
  • Encryption and other security measures can improve privacy, but they do not guarantee absolute confidentiality.
  • Users often rely on terms of service and privacy policies of platforms, which might include clauses allowing data usage or sharing.
  • Even private conversations can be exposed due to phishing attacks, malware, or inadequate security practices.
  • Thus, while the internet enables global and interactive communication, it is inaccurate to consider it always private.

Additional Information

  • It is asynchronous
    • Asynchronous communication refers to interactions where participants do not need to be present at the same time, such as emails, forums, and text messages.
    • The internet facilitates asynchronous communication, allowing users to respond at their convenience.
    • This characteristic makes the internet suitable for remote work, education, and collaborative projects.
  • It is interactive
    • The internet is inherently interactive, enabling real-time communication through chats, video calls, and collaborative tools.
    • It supports user engagement through features like comments, likes, and feedback on social media platforms and websites.
    • Interactive communication is essential for education, entertainment, and business applications.
  • It is global
    • The internet connects people across the world, enabling global communication, collaboration, and access to information.
    • It has revolutionized industries like trade, education, and media by removing geographical barriers.
    • Examples include international e-commerce platforms, remote work, and social media networks.

questions.question: Which of the following components is responsible for translating domain names (e.g., www.example.com) into IP addresses (e.g. 192.168.1.1) to enable communication over the internet?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following components is responsible for translating domain names (e.g., www.example.com) into IP addresses (e.g. 192.168.1.1) to enable communication over the internet?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is DNS Server.

Key Points

  • DNS Server (Domain Name System Server):
    • Translates human-readable website addresses (like [invalid URL removed]) into machine-readable IP addresses (like 172.217.160.142).   
    • Enables users to access websites by their names instead of memorizing complex IP addresses.   
    • Plays a crucial role in how the internet functions.

Additional Information

  • Firewall:
    • Acts as a security barrier between your computer and the internet.   
    • Monitors incoming and outgoing network traffic, blocking malicious attempts to access your computer or network.   
    • Helps prevent unauthorized access, viruses, and other cyber threats.   
  • Modem:
    • Modulates and demodulates data signals.   
    • Converts digital data from your computer into analog signals for transmission over communication lines (like phone lines or cable lines).   
    • Enables your computer to connect to the internet through your internet service provider (ISP).   
  • Router:
    • Directs network traffic between different devices on a network.   
    • Connects multiple devices (like computers, smartphones, and smart home devices) to a single internet connection.   
    • Allows devices to communicate with each other within the network and with the internet

questions.question: Which of the following options in MS Word 365 means the page is oriented vertically?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following options in MS Word 365 means the page is oriented vertically?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Portrait.

Key Points

  • Portrait orientation means that the page is taller than it is wide, similar to a standard book or document.
  • It is the default orientation in MS Word and most word processing applications.
  • Portrait orientation is typically used for text-heavy documents, such as letters, reports, and essays.
  • In MS Word 365, you can set the page orientation to Portrait by navigating to the Layout tab and selecting Orientation, then choosing Portrait.
  • Changing the orientation affects the entire document unless you specify different sections for different orientations.

Additional Information

  • Landscape Orientation
    • This orientation means the page is wider than it is tall, resembling a landscape picture.
    • It is often used for documents that require wide tables, charts, or diagrams.
    • In MS Word 365, you can set the page orientation to Landscape by navigating to the Layout tab and selecting Orientation, then choosing Landscape.
  • Page Setup
    • This is a feature in MS Word that allows you to customize the layout of your document, including orientation, margins, and paper size.
    • Accessed through the Layout tab, it provides comprehensive control over the document's appearance.
  • Default Settings
    • The default orientation setting in MS Word is Portrait.
    • Default settings can be changed in the Page Setup dialog box under the Layout tab.

questions.question: Which of the following is the core of an operating system?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the core of an operating system?
questions.solution: The kernel is the core of an operating system, serving as the essential center that provides basic services for all other parts of the OS. It acts as an interface between applications and hardware, managing processes, memory, file systems, device control, and networking. It is the first program loaded after the bootloader and controls all aspects of the OS. The kernel types include microkernel, monolithic kernel, hybrid kernel, exokernel, and nanokernel.

questions.question: What is the function of the ‘Superscript’ feature in Microsoft Word 365?
questions.questionHtml: What is the function of the ‘Superscript’ feature in Microsoft Word 365?

options.text: Makes the text bold and italic
options.html: Makes the text bold and italic

options.text: Adds a line under the text
options.html: Adds a line under the text

options.text: Makes the text larger and below the baseline
options.html: Makes the text larger and below the baseline

options.text: Makes the text smaller and above the baseline
options.html: Makes the text smaller and above the baseline

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Makes the text smaller and above the baseline.

Key Points

  • The "Superscript" feature in Microsoft Word 365 is a text formatting tool that allows you to raise the selected characters slightly above the baseline of the normal text.   
  • Its function and common uses:
    • Appearance: Superscripted text appears smaller than the surrounding text and is positioned higher, giving it a distinct visual appearance.   
    • Common Uses:
    • Mathematical Expressions:
    • Exponents: For example, "x²" (where the "2" is superscripted to indicate "x squared").   
    • Chemical Formulas: Representing chemical compounds with superscripts for charges or isotopes.   
    • Footnotes and Endnotes:
    • Displaying small, raised numbers or symbols to indicate references or additional information.   
    • Ordinal Numbers:
    • Representing ordinal numbers like "1st," "2nd," "3rd," where the "st," "nd," and "rd" are superscripted.   
    • Trademarks and Symbols:
    • Displaying symbols like ® (registered trademark), ™ (trademark), and © (copyright) as superscripts.
  • Units of Measurement:
    • Representing units like degrees Celsius (°C) or Fahrenheit (°F) with the degree symbol as a superscript.
    • How to Use the Superscript Feature in Word 365:
    • Using the Ribbon:
    • Select the text you want to format as superscript.
    • Go to the "Home" tab in the Ribbon.
    • In the "Font" group, click the "Superscript" button.
    • Using the Keyboard Shortcut:
    • Select the text you want to format as superscript.
    • Press and hold the Ctrl key, Shift key, and the "+" key simultaneously.

questions.question: Which of the following is a small piece of software that uses computer networks and security holes to replicate itself?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is a small piece of software that uses computer networks and security holes to replicate itself?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Worm.

Key Points

  •  Worm 
    • A worm is a small piece of software that uses computer networks and security holes to replicate itself.
    • A copy of the worm scans the network for another machine that has a specific security hole.
    • Worm Uses computer networks and security holes to replicate itself.
    • Many worms are designed only to spread and do not attempt to change the systems they pass through.
    • The first-ever computer worm was devised to be anti-virus software.

Additional Information

  •  Trojan horse
    • A Trojan horse is a type of malicious code or software that looks legitimate but takes control of your computer.
    • A Trojan is designed to damage, disrupt, steal, or in general, inflict some other harmful action on your data or network.
    • A Trojan acts as a bona fide application or file to trick you.
  • Application
    • An application program is a computer program designed to carry out a specific task other than one relating to the operation of the computer itself, typically to be used by end-users.
    • Applications may be bundled with the computer and its system software or published separately and may be coded as proprietary, open-source, or projects.
  • Operating System
    • An operating system is a software program required to manage and operate a computing device like smartphones, tablets, computers, supercomputers, web servers, cars, network towers, etc.
    • It is the operating system that eliminates the need to know coding language to interact with computing devices.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the Two - Factor Authentication (2FA)?

options.html: A technique for organising files and folders on a PC

options.html: A tool for optimising system resources

options.html: A security measure to prevent physical damage to a PC

questions.solution: Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) involves using two different credentials to verify a user's identity, typically something the user knows (password) and something the user has (mobile device or hardware token). This additional layer of verification enhances security and makes unauthorized access more difficult. Common 2FA methods include SMS-based codes, authenticator apps, and biometric methods. 2FA is a subset of multi-factor authentication (MFA) and is widely used in online banking, email services, and corporate environments to reduce the risk of identity theft, phishing attacks, and other cyber threats. Popular tools include Google Authenticator and YubiKey.

questions.question: Which of the following is an address on the world wide web that is used to access specific web resources and is the specific path to a resource?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is an address on the world wide web that is used to access specific web resources and is the specific path to a resource?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Uniform resource locator.

Key Points

  • Uniform Resource Locator (URL) is the specific address used to access web resources on the internet.
  • A URL consists of several components, including the protocol, domain name, path, and sometimes query parameters.
  • Examples of URLs include https://www.example.com or ftp://ftp.example.com/file.txt.
  • URLs are essential for navigating and accessing various resources on the World Wide Web efficiently.

Additional Information

  • Hyperlink:
    • A hyperlink is a reference or navigation element in a document that links to another section of the same document or to another document.
    • It is typically implemented using the anchor tag () in HTML.
      • Hyperlinks are clickable and usually appear as underlined text or images.
    • Web Server:
      • A web server is a computer system that hosts websites and serves web pages to users over the internet.
      • It uses protocols like HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) to communicate with web browsers.
      • Popular web servers include Apache, Nginx, and Microsoft Internet Information Services (IIS).
    • Web Pages:
      • A web page is a document on the World Wide Web that is identified by a unique URL.
      • Web pages are typically written in HTML and may contain text, images, videos, and other multimedia elements.
      • Web pages are the fundamental building blocks of websites.
    • Uniform Resource Locator (URL):
      • A URL is the address used to access specific resources on the internet.
      • It consists of several components: protocol (e.g., http, https, ftp), domain name (e.g., www.example.com), path (e.g., /path/to/resource), and possibly query parameters.
      • URLs are essential for the identification and retrieval of web resources.

questions.question: Which of the following is used when the sender does NOT want one or more of the recipients to know that someone else was copied on the message?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is used when the sender does NOT want one or more of the recipients to know that someone else was copied on the message?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is BCC.

Key Points

  • BCC stands for Blind Carbon Copy, which means that the recipients in the BCC field are hidden from each other and the main recipients.
  • When you send an email using BCC, the recipients included in the BCC field do not know who else has received the email.
  • This feature is particularly useful when you want to maintain the privacy of the recipients or avoid exposing their email addresses to each other.
  • BCC can also be used to send a copy of an email to someone discreetly without informing the main recipients.

Additional Information

  • From: This field indicates who is sending the email. It contains the sender's email address and possibly their name.
  • To: This field is used to specify the primary recipients of the email. The email addresses entered here are visible to all recipients.
  • CC: CC stands for Carbon Copy. The email addresses entered in this field are visible to all recipients. It is used when you want to send a copy of the email to additional recipients apart from the primary ones.
  • BCC: BCC stands for Blind Carbon Copy. The email addresses entered in this field are not visible to the other recipients. This is used when you want to send a copy of the email to someone without disclosing their email address to the other recipients.

Additional Information

questions.question: What is the default page orientation in Microsoft Word 365?
questions.questionHtml: What is the default page orientation in Microsoft Word 365?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Portrait.

Key Points

  • The default page orientation in Microsoft Word 365 is Portrait.
  • Portrait orientation is taller than it is wide, making it suitable for most documents.
  • This is the most commonly used orientation for text-heavy documents like letters, reports, and essays.
  • Users can change the page orientation to Landscape if needed, which is wider than it is tall.

Additional Information

  • Page Orientation:
    • Page orientation refers to the direction in which a document is displayed or printed.
    • There are two primary orientations: Portrait and Landscape.
    • Portrait Orientation: This is the vertical orientation where the height of the page is greater than the width.
    • Landscape Orientation: This is the horizontal orientation where the width of the page is greater than the height.
    • Microsoft Word allows users to switch between these orientations based on their document needs.
  • Changing Page Orientation:
    • To change the page orientation in Microsoft Word, go to the "Layout" tab on the ribbon.
    • Click on "Orientation" and choose either "Portrait" or "Landscape".
    • This can be applied to the entire document or a selected section.
  • Use Cases for Different Orientations:
    • Portrait: Suitable for standard text documents, letters, articles, and reports.
    • Landscape: Often used for presentations, charts, tables, and graphics-heavy documents.

questions.question: Which of the following features in MS Excel 365 involves setting the system to adjust cells to fit their contents automatically so that all the information is visible?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following features in MS Excel 365 involves setting the system to adjust cells to fit their contents automatically so that all the information is visible?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is AutoFit.

Key Points

  • AutoFit in MS Excel automatically adjusts the width of a column or the height of a row to fit the contents of the cells.
  • This feature helps in making sure that all the data within a cell is visible without needing to manually adjust the size of the cell.
  • It can be applied to a single column/row or multiple columns/rows at once.
  • Using AutoFit is particularly useful when dealing with large datasets where manually adjusting cell size would be time-consuming.

Additional Information

  • Fit Sheet on One Page
    • This option is used in the printing settings of Excel to fit an entire sheet onto a single page for printing.
    • It scales the content of the sheet so that all columns and rows fit on one page, which may make the content smaller and harder to read.
  • Cell Width
    • Cell width refers to the width of a single cell or a range of cells in an Excel sheet.
    • It can be adjusted manually by dragging the border of the column header or by specifying the width in the column width dialog box.
  • Fit to Cell
    • This is not a standard term or feature in MS Excel. It might be confused with the AutoFit feature.

questions.question: In MS Excel 365 what is the cell address of the cell two columns to the right and three rows down from cell D7?
questions.questionHtml: In MS Excel 365 what is the cell address of the cell two columns to the right and three rows down from cell D7?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is F10.

Key Points

  • The cell address two columns to the right and three rows down from cell D7 is F10.
  • Explanation:
  • Starting Point: We begin at cell D7.
  • Columns to the Right: To move two columns to the right, we increment the column letter by 2.
  • Column D + 2 columns = Column F
  • Rows Down: To move three rows down, we increment the row number by 3.
  • Row 7 + 3 rows = Row 10
  • Combining these movements:
  • Starting from cell D7, we move to the right two columns, reaching column F.
  • Then, we move down three rows, reaching row 10.
  • Therefore, the final cell address is F10.

questions.question: Which of the following is the purpose of the "Zoom" icon in Microsoft Word 365?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the purpose of the "Zoom" icon in Microsoft Word 365?

options.text: To adjust the visual appearance of our document to suit our reading or editing needs
options.html: To adjust the visual appearance of our document to suit our reading or editing needs

options.text: To change the document's page layout
options.html: To change the document's page layout

questions.solution:
The correct answer is to adjust the visual appearance of our document to suit our reading or editing needs.

Key Points

  • The Zoom icon in Microsoft Word 365 is used to control the magnification level of our document, making it larger or smaller on the screen.
  • It helps in adjusting the document view to make reading or editing more comfortable depending on our preference.
  • We can zoom in to get a closer view of the text or zoom out to see more of the page layout at once.
  • This feature is particularly useful when working with detailed documents or when we have vision difficulties.

Additional Information

  • Zoom Slider: Located at the bottom right corner of the Word window, this slider allows us to quickly adjust the zoom level by dragging the slider or clicking the plus (+) or minus (-) buttons.
  • Zoom Dialog Box: We can access more zoom options by clicking on the percentage value next to the zoom slider or by selecting "Zoom" from the "View" tab. This dialog box provides predefined zoom levels, a custom zoom option, and settings to fit the document to the window width, page width, or select multiple pages view.
  • Reading Mode: This feature optimizes the document layout for easier reading, removing unnecessary visual elements and adjusting the zoom level to fit the screen. We can activate it from the "View" tab or the status bar.
  • Print Layout vs. Web Layout: The Zoom feature works in conjunction with different layout views. In Print Layout, we see the document as it would appear when printed, while in Web Layout, the document adapts to fit the screen width, useful for documents intended for online viewing.
  • Page Width and Text Width: Options in the Zoom dialog allow us to fit the document to the width of the page or the width of the text, providing flexibility in how we view our content.

questions.question: Application software includes a variety of programs that are designed to meet the information processing needs of _______________.
questions.questionHtml: Application software includes a variety of programs that are designed to meet the information processing needs of _______________.
questions.solution: End users are the primary beneficiaries of application software, which is designed to help them perform specific tasks like word processing, web browsing, and data management. Although roles like programmers and team leaders may use this software, it is primarily created with end users in mind. Examples include Microsoft Office, Adobe Photoshop, and Google Chrome. System software, unlike application software, manages system resources and provides a platform for application software to run. Examples of system software are operating systems like Windows, macOS, and Linux. Application software is generally more user-friendly and accessible to non-technical users.

questions.question: Sir Tim Berners-Lee - a British computer scientist invented the revolutionary World Wide Web in ______.
questions.questionHtml: Sir Tim Berners-Lee - a British computer scientist invented the revolutionary World Wide Web in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1990.

Key Points

  • Tim Berners-Lee, a British computer scientist, generally credited as the inventor of the World Wide Web.
  • The development of the World Wide Web was begun in 1989 by Tim Berners-Lee and his colleagues at CERN, an international scientific organization based in Geneva, Switzerland. 
  • In 2004 he was awarded a knighthood by Queen Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom and the inaugural Millennium Technology Prize by the Finnish Technology Award Foundation.

Additional Information

Invention Founder(s)
Telephone Alexander Graham Bell
Electricity Benjamin Franklin
Penicillin Alexander Fleming
Theory of Relativity Albert Einstein
Internet Vinton Cerf and Bob Kahn
DNA Structure James Watson and Francis Crick
Microscope Zacharias Janssen
Printing Press Johannes Gutenberg
X-rays Wilhelm Conrad Roentgen
Steam Engine James Watt

 

NOTE: -

  • Tim Berners-Lee indeed began working on the idea for the World Wide Web in 1989 while at CERN, the European physics research center. However, the first successful communication between a web browser and a server via the Internet happened on December 25, 1990. Because the options provided do not include 1989, the closest accurate option would be:

1990

This represents the year when the World Wide Web became a functioning entity. However, if 1989 were an option, it would be the most accurate choice to represent when Berners-Lee first started developing the concept.
